standard_prerequisites.name: C2-closeness of contact forms
standard_prerequisites.statement: lambda C2-close to lambda_0 implies nu and omega close in the corresponding norms.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis and the first remark of the proof at source line 1507.

standard_prerequisites.name: Moser's trick with boundary conditions
standard_prerequisites.statement: One looks for an isotopy fixing the boundary whose pull-backs equal omega_0, generated by a vector field solving X_t interior omega_t = nu_0 - nu + d f_t.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the framework of the whole proof, source lines 1509-1518.

standard_prerequisites.name: Collar model on the annulus
standard_prerequisites.statement: On a collar A_C the forms can be written with the functions h_1, h_2, h_3 and the differential identity partial_r(r h_2) - partial_s h_1 = r(h_3 - 1).
standard_prerequisites.use: They are used to choose f and to estimate R_t, source lines 1525-1577.

core_obligations: Note that C2-closeness of lambda to lambda_0 gives smallness of nu - nu_0 and omega - omega_0, and use the retained transversality assumption to see that omega is symplectic in the interior with the same orientation, so the interpolating forms omega_t are symplectic and uniformly C1-close (source line 1507).

Set up Moser's trick: look for an isotopy fixing the boundary with kappa_t^* omega_t = omega_0 and derive the equation d(X interior omega_t + nu - nu_0) = 0, then choose X_t by X_t interior omega_t = nu_0 - nu + d f_t with a C2-small f to be determined so that X_t extends smoothly and vanishes on the boundary (source lines 1509-1523).

On each collar component use the retained collar equation and the retained normalisation lemma's first two parts to write nu_0 - nu and omega in terms of smooth functions h_1, h_2, h_3, note their smallness, and record the differential identity (source lines 1525-1539).

Compute the components R_t, S_t of X_t and choose f with f identically zero near the outer part of the collar and equal to minus the integral of h_1 near the boundary, then show S_t vanishes and R_t = -r h_4/(t(h_3-1)+1) with h_4 C0-small (source lines 1540-1577).

Conclude that X_t is C1-small, extends smoothly, vanishes on the boundary, and that its flow kappa_t fixes the boundary and pulls omega_t back to omega_0; then kappa := kappa_1 has the required properties and is C1-close to the identity (source lines 1578-1579).

proof_roadmap.step: Closeness and symplecticity of the interpolating forms.
Moser's trick and the choice of the defining equation for X_t.
Collar computation of nu_0 - nu, omega and the differential identity.
Choice of f and the estimates making X_t small and boundary-vanishing.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `l:pullback_to_nu0` at source lines 1501-1504: if lambda is C2-close enough to lambda_0 then there is a diffeomorphism kappa fixing the boundary with kappa^* omega = omega_0, and kappa is C1-close to the identity as lambda approaches lambda_0. The author's proof (source lines 1506-1580) is a complete Moser-trick construction on a surface with boundary: it first checks that the interpolating forms are symplectic with the right orientation and uniformly close (line 1507), sets up the isotopy equation d(X interior omega_t + nu - nu_0) = 0 and chooses the defining equation for X_t with a function f still to be determined (lines 1509-1523), computes in collar coordinates the structure functions h_1, h_2, h_3 together with the differential identity they satisfy (lines 1525-1539), chooses f explicitly as minus the integral of h_1 near the boundary and zero further out, and then estimates the two components of X_t, obtaining S_t = 0 and a formula for R_t with a C0-small numerator that makes X_t C1-small, smoothly extendable and boundary-vanishing (lines 1540-1577); the flow then gives the conclusion (lines 1578-1579). The statement contains only the existence and the convergence, and the whole quantitative part is invisible in it.
